title: Fonctions L / Équation fonctionnelle des fonctions L (cas géométrique) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is the 'geometric case' of the functional equation of L-functions, essentially the framework of Grothendieck's Bourbaki talk 279 (1964) and SGA 5. Let X be proper and smooth of dimension n over F_q, with Frobenius f. Let E be a lisse l-adic sheaf with a perfect pairing E⊗E → Q_l(-p), i.e. Ě ≅ E(p) globally. Then Poincaré duality makes H^i(X̄,E) dual to H^{2n-i}(X̄,E)(n+p). This gives a functional equation L_E(1/(q^{n+p}t)) = ε'(E)·(const)·t^{χ}·L_E(t). The pairs (H^i, H^{2n-i}) with i≠n contribute only squares to the sign. So the sign ε'(E) is governed by the middle group H^n(X̄,E), whose weight is n+p (the underbrace reads 'poids n+p'). Its cup-product pairing is (-1)^{n+p}-symmetric, and Frobenius multiplies it by q^{n+p}.

Case n+p odd. The form is alternating and non-degenerate, so b_n = dim H^n is even and (-1)^{b_n} = 1. The normalized Frobenius f/q^{(n+p)/2} is symplectic, so its determinant is +1. This is the 'raisonnement du cours de Serre'. Hence ε'(E) = 1.

Case n+p even. The form is symmetric and the normalized Frobenius is orthogonal, so its eigenvalues λ ≠ ±1 come in pairs λ, 1/λ. Let ε_1 and ε_{-1} be the multiplicities of the eigenvalues +1 and -1. Then:
- (-1)^{b_n} = (-1)^{ε_1+ε_{-1}};
- the determinant sign is ε(E) = (-1)^{ε_{-1}};
- so the total sign is ε'(E) = (-1)^{ε_1}.
This generalizes the classical fact that the sign in the functional equation of the zeta function of an even-dimensional variety is (-1)^N, with N the multiplicity of the eigenvalue q^{n/2} on middle cohomology.

Finally the page notes what happens outside the favourable case (X smooth, E lisse, Ě ≅ E(p)). The dual D(E), in the sense of what later became Verdier duality, is no longer simply a twist of E. The functional equation (1) then relates two different functions, L_{DE} and L_E. This is the general form of the functional equation in SGA 5.
errors: The sign statement tacitly refers to the normalized Frobenius f/q^{(n+p)/2}, since 'valeur propre 1 (-1)' only makes sense after normalization. Purity is not needed: the duality pairing alone pairs λ with q^{n+p}/λ.
The symmetry type of the pairing E⊗E → Q_l(-p) is assumed to be (-1)^p-symmetric, as for sheaves of geometric origin. The page uses this implicitly.
'H^n(X̄,F)' is presumably a slip for E.

ideas.what: Sign of the functional equation of L_E for self-dual lisse E: +1 if n+p is odd (symplectic case), (-1)^{multiplicity of eigenvalue +q^{(n+p)/2}} if n+p is even (orthogonal case)
ideas.modern_name: Root number / sign of the functional equation for self-dual (orthogonal/symplectic) l-adic sheaves
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Weil, Serre, Grothendieck); for the zeta-function case it appears in standard treatments of the Weil conjectures, and the general orthogonal/symplectic dichotomy is in Deligne's work
ideas.where_published: Likely implicit in Bourbaki exposé 279 (1964) and in SGA 5; not sure the explicit sign formula appears there

ideas.what: Determinant of a symplectic similitude is positive (the argument from Serre's course)
In general (X singular, or E not self-dual up to twist) the functional equation relates L_E and L_{DE}, with D the duality functor
ideas.modern_name: Functional equation via Verdier/Grothendieck duality for constructible sheaves

deep.surprise_reason: A clean but standard computation of the sign of the functional equation in the self-dual case, plus a remark leading to the L_E / L_{DE} functional equation. All of this is well known and in Grothendieck's own published framework.
transcription_corrections: The underbrace under H^n(X̄,E) on line 1 reads 'poids n+p' (weight n+p), not 'variété n+p'. Also the group is H^n(X̄,E), not H^{n+p}.
'X lisse, E et duales' is more likely 'X lisse, E lisse (localement libre)', followed by 'Ě globalement isomorphe à E(p)'.
The insertion above line 7 reads roughly '(produit des 2 produits)' or similar; the sense is that only the product of the two signs can be determined.
